title: VALORIZATION OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES AS ALTERNATIVE LINER MATERIALS: COMPRESSIBILITY AND SHEAR STRENGTH
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable waste containment systems has intensified interest in replacing conventional clay liners with alternative geomaterials derived from industrial by-products. This study addresses this gap by investigating the hydro-mechanical behavior of soil mixtures incorporating water treatment sludge (WTS), vegetal biomass ash (VBA), granitic mining waste (GMW), and blast furnace slag (BFS), with emphasis on their potential applicability as liner materials. A comprehensive experimental program was conducted, including one-dimensional oedometric consolidation, expansibility and swelling assessment, and consolidated undrained (CU) triaxial testing for mixtures containing up to 20% WTS and VBA, and up to 50% GMW and BFS, by dry mass. Optimized mixtures which achieved hydraulic conductivity lower than 10 -9 m/s were WTS15% with compression index of 0.129, cohesion of 25 kPa and internal friction angle of 31º, VBA10% with 0.090, 10kPa and 29º, GMW50% with 0.118, 0kPa and 35º, and BFS25% with 0.066, 0kPa and 35º, respectively. Additionally, those mixtures comprised swelling pressure lower than 25kPa and free swell lower than 15%. The results reveal two contrasting behavioral trends. Mixtures containing ash, mining waste, and slag exhibit reduced compressibility, lower swelling potential, increased shear strength, associated with improved particle packing and, in the case of slag, latent hydraulic reactivity. title: From Diagnosis to Digital Execution: AI-Enabled Materials Management for High-Intensity Operations
journal: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
abstract: Abstract In high-intensity energy operations, material availability depends on more than the accuracy of an enterprise resource planning inventory balance. A component may be recorded as available and still be unusable because its location, condition, certification or readiness for the work cannot be confirmed. The resulting searches, expediting, emergency purchasing and workarounds create a form of operational friction that is often managed locally until the cumulative effect appears in maintenance delay, lost productivity, excess working capital or avoidable logistics activity. A diagnostic-led transformation method is presented using practitioner evidence from energy and other asset-intensive operations. The method combines site engagement, benchmarking, value stream mapping, direct process observation and data analysis to identify where material flow is breaking down. Critical-to-quality requirements are then translated into a future-state operating model before the digital architecture is selected. Typical execution controls include master-data remediation, barcode or Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) identification, mobile warehouse tasks, two-way Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) integration, automated exception workflows, supplier-performance visibility, risk-based inventory policy and AI-enabled optimisation where the data and decision are suitable for probabilistic modelling. title: Toward Durable Prosthetic Feet: Mechanical and Tribological Evaluation of Polyurethane Elastomers
journal: Advance Sustainable Science Engineering and Technology
abstract: Elastomeric materials play a crucial role in determining the durability, comfort, and service life of prosthetic feet. Although various elastomers have been explored for this application, systematic evaluation of polyurethane formulations that integrate mechanical and tribological performance remains limited. This study investigates two types of polyurethane elastomers (A70 and A80) with different polyol–isocyanate ratios to identify an optimal formulation for prosthetic foot applications. Mechanical properties were evaluated through tensile, tear, hardness, and density tests, while friction and wear behavior were assessed using a pin-on-disk tribometer. A commercial prosthetic foot elastomer available in the Indonesian market was used as a benchmark. The results show that A80-based formulations generally provide superior tensile and tear strength compared to A70 variants. Among all specimens, A80-3 exhibits the lowest wear volume and stable friction performance, while maintaining hardness comparable to the commercial product. Although its density remains higher than the benchmark, the improved wear resistance indicates potential for extended service life. These findings offer practical guidance for durability-oriented material selection in the development of cost-efficient prosthetic feet.

title: The Imperfection Paradox: A Syllogistic Critique of Modernity, Enforced Blindness, and the Thermodynamic Return of the Physical Voice
abstract: “The Imperfection Paradox” introduces a multi-tiered syllogistic framework analyzing the structural friction between modern techno-capitalist abstractions and absolute physical limits. The preprint maps out a critical trajectory of modernity operating as a closed cybernetic architecture driven by an imperative of infinite scaling and total optimization. To maintain its trajectory, this technosphere constructs digital and financial abstractions that treat energy and capital as infinitely malleable variables, producing a dangerous "systemic decoupling" from its material foundations. The text details how complex networks enforce an internal state of absolute blindness ("You are not to know you are imperfect"), intentionally severing feedback loops to suppress internal errors and thermodynamic realities. However, because every byte of processed data remains tethered to material resource extraction and energy grids, this expanding "decoupling gap" eventually hits an immutable boundary. The analysis culminates in a structural diagnostic of terminal systemic realization—the point of "entropic convergence" where the abstract system develops a physical voice ("a mouth") and is forced into absolute thermodynamic silence, collapsing virtual acceleration into physical reality. The manuscript concludes with an integrated pedagogical framework, providing a graduate-level seminar syllabus and introductory lecture script designed to operationalize these concepts.

title: Experimental Optical Microscope Dataset for Tribological Characterization of Engineering Steels under Dry Reciprocating Sliding Conditions
abstract: The Steel_Wear_Morphology_Dataset comprises optical microscopic images of wear surfaces from 15 different steel materials, organized according to their respective steel designations (e.g., SAE4140_S1). Within the main dataset folder, each steel category is further divided into folders representing the experimental test conditions (A1-A6). Each condition folder contains separate Before Test and After Test directories, which are further organized into Bar and Pin subfolders corresponding to the two tribological contact surfaces. For each experimental condition, the dataset contains: Before Test: Six microscopic images for each Bar and Pin specimen. After Test: Ten microscopic images for each Bar and Pin specimen. All images are provided in TIF format and are sequentially numbered (e.g., 1.TIF, 2.TIF, 3.TIF). The microscopic images were acquired using optical microscopy at 100× magnification with a 10× objective lens and a resolution of 2160 × 1620 pixels. Representative images were captured from multiple locations along the wear track to provide a comprehensive characterization of surface morphology, wear scars, and damage features. In addition to the microscopy images, the accompanying Supporting Information includes the corresponding experimental parameters, such as the coefficient of friction (COF), sliding distance (s), and other relevant testing conditions. title: Current-driven Magnetic Skyrmions for Encoding/Storing Information: Manipulation and Dynamics in Nanoscale Structures
abstract: This dissertation investigates the dynamics of current-driven magnetic skyrmions, topological solitons in magnetic materials with broken spatial inversion symmetry, for low-power spintronic applications like racetrack memory and multilevel data storage. Skyrmions’ small size and low driving current requirements make them promising information carriers. The research examines skyrmion motion under driving currents, pinning effects, and thermal fluctuations, using numerical simulations (Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation), analytical studies (Thiele equation), and theoretical modeling to design novel data storage devices. The study analyzes skyrmion motion amidst pinning potentials from material imperfections. Simulations reveal that thermal fluctuations vary with damping: acting as a frictional force at low damping or a driving force aiding depinning at high damping. The Thiele equation quantifies this, though its accuracy wanes at low temperatures with pinning. The skyrmion Hall angle, influenced by current and pinning, provides insights for ambient-condition devices. These findings underpin a proposed multilevel data storage device, where controlled current positions skyrmions at pinning sites for high-density, low-power encoding. The research also explores altermagnetic (ATM) skyrmions, which exhibit d-wave symmetry via exchange-driven spin splitting. title: From Failure Forensics to Field Transformation: Doubling MTBF in Pumpjack Tubing Through Integrated MIC and Wear Mitigation
journal: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
abstract: Abstract This case study investigates lifecycle-driven strategies for enhancing downhole production tubing integrity in mature oilfields, with a focus on cost-effective risk reduction. During a campaign to increase the number of wells count, a significant increase in tubing leaks was observed across multiple new wells (deviated and horizontal), primarily attributed to two failure modes: external corrosion, and internal wear caused by rod friction. Comprehensive root cause analysis, including forensic laboratory testing of metal and fluid samples, confirmed that CO2 corrosion was the principal driver of external corrosion, accompanied by MIC as a significant contributor with sulphate-reducing bacteria and other microbial activity accelerating localized metal loss at specific well depths. Internal wear was linked to non-centrical rod movement in deviated well sections, resulting in progressive material loss and leaks. Targeted mitigation strategies were implemented, including the selective application of fiberglass cloth and resin external coatings at high-risk zones, installation of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) inner liners to address internal wear, and the deployment of adaptive chemical injection programs to control bacterial activity. Field trials demonstrated substantial improvements, with mean time between failures (MTBF) increasing from 484 to 974 days and estimated operational expenditure (OPEX) savings of USD 27.5 million (avoided workover cost). title: Macro-micro_HBS_small2large_strain
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: # Hydrate-Bearing Sand (HBS) DEM Research Repository This repository contains a collection of discrete-element-method (DEM) simulations and analysis scripts for hydrate-bearing granular materials. The workflow is built around Yade-based triaxial simulations, parameter sweeps for hydrate morphology and stiffness, and a set of microstructural/post-processing tools used to inspect stress, porosity, connectivity, force anisotropy, and pore structure. The code is primarily research-oriented and is organized as a set of simulation drivers, parameter tables, and analysis utilities rather than a packaged software library. This is still a very initial version of the code, and the code structure is somewhat messy at the moment. title: Study on proppant-fiber cluster structure and settling characteristics for full-domain propped fracturing
journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
abstract: The concept of “full-domain propped fracturing” aims to improve fracture placement morphology by efficient placement in main fractures and hierarchical propping of multi-scale fractures, thereby effectively addressing the limitation of propped fracture volume in unconventional oil and gas reservoirs. Using proppant-fiber clusters instead of pure proppant as the basic transport units in fractures can effectively increase the lateral migration distance and vertical placement height of proppant in main fractures, serving as a key technical approach for achieving efficient fracture placement. This study constructed a physical model of proppant-fiber clusters through microstructural observations, static settling experiments, and dynamic transport experiments, and revealed the settling and placement patterns of cluster units within fractures. The results indicated that proppant-fiber clusters were a composite system jointly composed of a fiber framework that traps proppant particles, a filamentous network of friction reducer polymers, and sheet-like stabilizer structures. Characterization of cluster units and their size distributions revealed that increasing fiber mass fraction and length facilitated the formation of larger cluster units. Specifically, the average proppant placement height increased by 116.6% for a proppant mixture with a fiber mass fraction of 0.5% compared with that of pure proppant. title: Reply on CEC2
abstract: Abstract. Solver-coupled learning offers a structured alternative to direct state-to-state regression for global atmospheric forecasting, but its forecast quality depends on how accurately the embedded coefficient dynamics represent unresolved forcing and coarse-grid numerical effects. We represent these unresolved effects using a bounded transport-residual closure (BTRC) embedded in an explicit sub-stepping solver. Building on the reduced horizontal transport-coefficient dynamics of PASSAT, we separate a retained spherical advection–curvature operator from aggregate terms omitted, approximated, or numerically distorted by the reduced model, including pressure-gradient, Coriolis, frictional, subgrid, vertical-coupling, and discretization contributions. A graph network estimates a raw aggregate equation discrepancy, which is mapped through a scaled hyperbolic tangent to obtain the BTRC. The resulting closure is inserted into the coefficient-update pathway and modifies the transport coefficients used by subsequent atmospheric state updates. The bound limits the direct closure-induced coefficient increment per Euler sub-step to δtτ, providing a numerical safeguard against unconstrained learned forcing; it is not presented as a proof of global dynamical stability. The BTRC is shared across prognostic channels as a compact directional correction, while an auxiliary node-level gated wavelet branch refines multi-resolution graph features. title: A Case Study of Catastrophic Timing Gear Failure in a Multiphase Twin-Screw Pump
journal: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a field case study of a catastrophic timing-gear failure of a twin-screw multiphase pump, a production-critical positive-displacement pump used to boost unseparated flow stream consisting of oil, gas, and water. In this pump configuration, the external timing gears perform a vital function by maintaining accurate rotor phasing and preventing rotor-to-rotor contact while the screw elements handle highly variable multiphase service. The reliability of this arrangement depends not only on its design, but also on continuous reliable lubrication to the timing gears, bearings, and associated seal system. The pump unit was on standby mode before being returned to service and tripped on high motor current after startup. Following initial troubleshooting, the motor driver was decoupled and found satisfactory, while the pump was difficult to rotate, indicating internal mechanical lock-up. Subsequent workshop dismantling confirmed seized timing gears, jammed screw shafts, extensive thermal discoloration, rotor runout outside tolerance and crack indications on the screw flights outside-diameter. No abnormal vibration or temperature alarm was reported before the high-current trip, highlighting that the available protection responded only after severe mechanical distress had already developed. title: The Manual Transmission Paradigm in Deterministic AI Governance: Clutch-Granularity Control, Multi-Gear Algebraic Routing, and Road-Surface IP Sovereignty under Human-in-Command (HIC)
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Contemporary discourse surrounding generative artificial intelligence is polarized between passive external criticism and the naïve expectation of fully autonomous ("automatic transmission") execution. However, operating high-dimensional stochastic models during the current civilizational transition—analogous to shifting from horse-drawn carriages to mechanical powertrains—requires explicit, operator-driven kinematics. Waiting for zero-friction automation creates an insurmountable capability deficit relative to active practitioners who master direct mechanical engagement. title: The AI Organizational Magnifier Theory: How AI Amplifies Structures, Standards, and Consequences in Organizational Talent Decisions
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: While AI adoption in organizational talent decisions has accelerated dramatically, systematic failures have emerged that existing algorithmic bias frameworks cannot fully explain: candidates silently excluded without traceability, well-intentioned diversity policies executed to their literal extreme, critical review steps optimized away by efficiency logic, and exceptional candidates systematically filtered out by historically derived success templates. This paper proposes the AI Organizational Magnifier Theory, which argues that AI systems do not independently generate organizational defects but amplify pre-existing structural capability gaps, unbounded standards, and decision consequences. The theory's meta-concept frames AI as a Brake Remover: an agent that dismantles three natural organizational braking mechanisms—the self-limiting nature of weak execution capability, the physical speed ceiling of human processing, and the temporal buffer of organizational friction. Drawing on practitioner research across 20 years and 16 Asia-Pacific markets, and four in-depth case studies, the theory identifies three pillars of amplification (structural, standards, consequence) and nine original sub-concepts. The paper proposes the governance axiom Automate elimination; retain human judgment for selection and the Verify the Tail mechanism, operationalized through a Three Gates governance framework. title: Evaluation of performance and emissions of a diesel engine using dual aqueous ammonia -diesel fuel
abstract: Abstract The carbon footprint of fossil fuel application is a crucial indicator of the overall quantity of greenhouse gases discharged into the atmosphere. Sustainable replacements, such as aqueous ammonia, are viewed as a good approach to solve the shortage of conventional fuel, low-carbon fuels and address climate change. Emissions and performance of diesel engine running on dual fuel of diesel and aqueous ammonia were investigated. Ammonia and water were combined in volumetric amounts of 5, 10, and 15% to get around these adverse effects. Adding aqueous ammonia of 5, 10 and 15% to diesel boosted brake specific fuel consumption by 4, 7, and 13% at 75% of engine output power. Thermal efficiency of diesel and aqueous ammonia were decreased by 4, 7 and 13% when aqueous ammonia was added by 5, 10 and 15%. Aqueous ammonia of 5%, 10% and 15% demonstrated increases of 17, 32 and 42% in CO emissions about diesel, whereas the decreases in nitrogen oxides were 5, 10 and 15% in relation to diesel, respectively. At 100% of output power, increases in hydrocarbon emissions for 5%, 10%, and 15% aqueous ammonia were 10, 23, and 31% but carbon dioxide values were decreased by 6, 12, and 17% for diesel with aqueous ammonia compared to diesel oil. Increases of oxygen concentrations for 5%, 10% and 15% aqueous ammonia were 6, 8 and 10%, respectively at 75% of output power. title: Design, Fabrication, and Performance Evaluation of a Locally Developed Automotive Engine Test Bed Using a Hydraulic Water-Brake Dynamometer
journal: GPH-International Journal of Mechanical And Civil Engineering
abstract: Abstract The high cost of commercial automotive engine test facilities limits access to reliable engine performance testing equipment in many Nigerian tertiary institutions, thereby constraining practical engineering training and experimental research. This study aimed to design, construct and evaluate a locally fabricated automotive engine test bed incorporating a hydraulic water-brake dynamometer. The test bed was designed for four-cylinder petrol engines with displacement capacities of 1.2-2.0 L, a design power absorption rating of 90 kW and a maximum design torque of 220 N·m. The supporting frame was fabricated from mild steel, while torque was measured using a strain-gauge load cell mounted on a 500 mm moment arm. Engine speed was measured using an optical tachometer, and temperature and fuel-consumption measurements were incorporated into the instrumentation system. The test bed was evaluated using a Toyota 7A-FE, 1.8 L, four-cylinder petrol engine under full-load conditions between 1,000 and 5,500 rpm and at different throttle openings at 3,000 rpm. The results showed a maximum recorded torque of 135.5 N·m at 3,000 rpm and a maximum calculated brake power of approximately 56.0 kW at 5,000 rpm. During part-load testing, torque and brake power increased with increasing throttle opening. The reported direct material cost was ₦286,500, excluding labour and overheads.
